approach: Widen the planning gate in `Athena::dispatch` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs line 804-809). Add a small documented helper, `asks_for_failing_run(&Reading) -> bool`, true when any accepted Behavior criterion's text (lower-cased, whitespace collapsed) names a failing run without the fix. The phrases are `fails without the fix`, `fail without the fix`, `fails without the change` and `fails without the mechanism`. Pass `reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_failing_run(&reading)` to the existing `JobPlanConfig::plans`. `plans` keeps its `enabled && (All || hard)` rule, so `enabled = false` still plans nothing and `mode = "all"` is unchanged. The `!capability.pins_repo()` guard stays. A newly planned job follows the existing path (`plan_round`, accepted plan, `demonstration_records`, verifier brief), none of which change. Tests drive `Athena::go` with the fake agents in athena-core and athena-cli. Docs, CHANGELOG and config.rs doc comments state the rule. This revision rewrites the criterion 6 demonstration so it names what fails without the behavior: a named set of mutations of the gate, each caught by a named existing or new test.

decisions.choice: Put the trigger in a named `pub(crate) fn asks_for_failing_run(reading: &Reading) -> bool` in run/mod.rs. The gate passes `reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_failing_run(&reading)` to the existing `JobPlanConfig::plans`.
decisions.reason: The fault is the gate at mod.rs:804-809, which looks only at `hard_reason`. A doc-commented helper is what criterion 4 asks for. `enabled` and `mode` keep their meaning in config.rs, so `enabled = false` and `mode = "all"` behave as today. The reading is in scope at the gate, and run/mod.rs already holds helpers such as `planned_paths`.

rejected.option: Change the signature of `JobPlanConfig::plans` to take the reading or a second bool
rejected.why: It would touch the config tests (config.rs ~856 and ~1175-1181), which criterion 6 says must stay unchanged, and make config depend on reading text.

rejected.option: Set `hard_reason` on the reading when a criterion asks for a failing run
rejected.why: `hard_reason` also escalates the producer model and effort (reading.rs `producer_setting`, `producer_effort`) and is a reader output, so it would change which model builds the job.

rejected.option: Add a `fails_without` field to the reading's Criterion record
rejected.why: Out of scope: it changes a record schema and the round-trip test, and the reader would have to produce it.

rejected.option: Plan every job that has any Behavior criterion
rejected.why: Too broad: it would plan most easy jobs and undo the `hard` mode saving; criterion 2 requires ordinary easy jobs to skip planning.

decisions.choice: Match on lower-cased text with whitespace collapsed, against a const list of four phrases, for Behavior criteria only.
decisions.reason: The reading's Criterion has only `text` and `kind` (crates/athena-data/src/records.rs). The brief says criterion text naming 'fails without the fix'. Plan admission lets only behavior criteria carry fails_without (crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs ~152, ~210), so a Content criterion gains nothing from planning.

rejected.why: A content criterion cannot hold a fails_without demonstration under admission.rs, so planning it buys nothing.
It would match unrelated prose such as 'the build fails without a network'. Fixed phrases keep false triggers rare, and a false trigger costs only one planning round.

decisions.choice: Cover criteria 1 and 2 in both core run::tests and CLI job_plan.rs. Cover the demonstration record reaching the verifier only in the core test.
decisions.reason: Core tests install `demo_seam` and run a real revert copy (tests.rs ~3096-3105). The CLI fixture has no seam, so no demonstration record is produced there; the CLI test checks planning under the repository's real `[job_plan]` table.

rejected.option: Install the demo seam in CLI tests
rejected.why: `demo_seam` is a pub(crate) module of athena-core, so it would need a new public test-support export, more surface than the change needs.

decisions.choice: Edit config.rs doc comments only, on `PlanMode::Hard` and `JobPlanConfig::plans`.
decisions.reason: config.rs is a listed deliverable. Its docs say hard mode plans only a job whose reading is marked hard, which would be false after the change. No logic or serde shape changes.

rejected.why: The doc on `PlanMode::Hard` would be wrong and the deliverables list the file.

decisions.choice: Answer the finding on criterion 6 by splitting it into outcome gates plus named mutations of the gate. Each mutation is caught by a named test, so the demonstration states what fails without the behavior. The mutations are: (a) the criterion check dropped, (b) the gate widened to every Behavior criterion or every job, (c) `hard_reason` ignored.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6 is tagged [behavior], so its demonstration needs `fails_without`. The behavior it protects is that the widened gate leaves the mode semantics intact. The existing job_plan.rs tests at lines 1104 and 1161 and the new tests fail under those mutations.

rejected.option: Mark criterion 6 as a non-behavior check with fails_without null
rejected.why: The brief tags it [behavior], and Athena requires fails_without on a behavior demonstration.

Add `repo_with_hard_planning`, a criterion-rewrite wrapper over the reader, producer and verifier fakes, the plans-test, the stays-skipped test and the helper unit test.

Add two CLI tests under the repository's real `[job_plan]` table: an easy job with a 'fails without the fix' criterion is planned, and an ordinary easy job still skips planning. Existing tests stay unedited.
Section 9, after 'Planning for hard jobs only': state that a job whose accepted Behavior criterion names a failing run without the fix is planned even when judged easy, and why.
Add an entry under `[Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` naming the root cause (the gate looked only at `hard_reason`, so demonstrations never ran for easy jobs) and the fix.
Doc-comment edits only on `PlanMode::Hard` and `JobPlanConfig::plans`, so they match the widened gate. No logic or serde change.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan` and `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. Confirm the existing mode tests in job_plan.rs (lines 1104 and 1161) pass without edits.

risks.risk: The phrase match over free text can fire on a criterion that mentions the phrase without really asking for a failing run, or miss a differently worded ask.
risks.mitigation: A false trigger costs one planning round on a job that did not need it. It is limited to Behavior criteria with fixed phrases, and `enabled = false` still switches planning off. Preflight reserves the planning budget before anything is committed, so an unaffordable job is held, not half-run.

risks.risk: The core test changes the criterion text in the reader fake, but the base-script producer and verifier fakes echo the old `CRITERION`, so the job could be sent back or rejected.
risks.mitigation: The wrapper rewrites the criterion text in all three fakes: reader output, producer `criteria_check` and verifier `criteria`, following the existing `run_planned_behavior` pattern near tests.rs:632. The new test asserts the job lands, so a mismatch shows up as a failed job.

risks.risk: The demonstration yields a record only if the plan's command is a plain `cargo test ...` and the seam is installed; a typo would make the prompt assertion fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The test reuses `demo_seam::install` and the `README_TEST` script as `run_demonstration_job` does (tests.rs ~3096-3125). The demonstration command is a plain `cargo test --locked demo` under the seam, so no real cargo runs.

risks.risk: `repo_with_config` strips the `[job_plan]` table from athena.toml, and a wrong key would fail the config parse (`deny_unknown_fields`).
risks.mitigation: Build the hard-mode repo with `repo_with_config` and add its own `[job_plan]` table, with the exact text from `repo_with_planning` but `mode = "hard"`.

risks.risk: Reviewers may read the criterion matcher as a new refusal or matching rule that needs a corpus case.
risks.mitigation: The change adds no refusal rule and no record, so the corpus and `check_record_file` are unaffected. The corpus test is still run as a guard in the outcome check.

risks.risk: The criterion 6 outcome check could be read as passing trivially.
risks.mitigation: The criterion 6 demonstration names the mutations that make it fail (always-true gate, ignored mode or enabled, malformed code) and the unchanged tests that catch each, so it is not satisfied by activity alone.

demonstrations.method: Core test `an_easy_job_whose_behavior_criterion_fails_without_the_fix_is_planned_and_the_verifier_gets_the_revert_run`. It uses `repo_with_hard_planning` (a `repo_with_config` call with `[job_plan] enabled = true, mode = "hard"`). A wrapper script around `planning_script(vec![behavior_plan(seam)], vec![accepting_critique()], calls)` rewrites reader `acceptance_criteria[0]` to `{kind: behavior, text: "a test that fails without the fix covers the demo"}` with no `hard_reason`. The same wrapper rewrites the producer `criteria_check[0].criterion` and verifier `criteria[0].criterion` to that text, so report and verdict match the reading. It installs `demo_seam::install(Rc::new(|_| vec!["sh","-c",README_TEST]))`, as `run_demonstration_job` does (tests.rs ~3096). It drives `athena.ask` then `athena.go`, reads the verifier prompt from `Calls`, and asserts roles Reader, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier. It also asserts `job-plan-1.json` exists at HEAD (`Git::at(repo.path()).path_exists`) and that the verifier prompt contains `fails-without-1`, `failed without the fix (exit 1)` and `test demo ... FAILED`. CLI test `an_easy_job_with_a_fails_without_criterion_is_planned_under_the_repository_hard_mode` uses `repository_job_plan_config()` and a `Scenario` with `reading["acceptance_criteria"][1]["text"]` naming 'fails without the fix'. It asserts roles Reader, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier and `job-plan-1.json` and `critique-1.json` at head.

open_questions: User: Should a Behavior criterion that says 'tests fail without the fix' (plural) or 'fails without this change' also trigger planning? The plan lists only `fails without the fix`, `fail without the fix`, `fails without the change` and `fails without the mechanism`. The brief names only the first; widening the list is one line in the helper.
